Five months later in January 2025, her dark relationship with a teenage pupil was discovered and reported to the police.

She was immediately suspended, and later fired from the school and banned from the grounds.

However, less than a month later, security cams show Johnson-Swartz picking up the student from school and driving away with him.

She was charged with felony kidnapping and arrested, before being released the next day to return to court at a later date.



Johnson-Swartz then stalked the student to back-to-back concerts of one of the bands they had shared in their playlists.

The teen later told investigators: “It was really weird. I was going there expecting to have a really great time.

“And then I just see her in front of the line, like 30 feet up”

In one interview, the teen said his former teacher cornered him and said: “Just say you love me”.

The student said they were not surprised the 45-year-old struggled to stay away, saying she is an “unstable woman” who had “already ruined her life, and […] keeps just making it worse.”



The former teacher was arrested a second time, and denied bail.

Douglas County District Attorney George Brauchler said Johnson-Swartz is a “predator” who will now have to “live with that label for decades”.

News.title: I knew the Mafia’s darkest serial killers who blowtorched privates off – I’ll never forget one madman’s sick stunt
News.content:
LOUIS Ferrante hijacked terrified truck drivers at gun point, was accused of shooting a fellow fraudster and was eventually slapped with a 13-year jail sentence after his underworld career was busted.

But, having made his name working for Mafia lords like John Gotti, his crimes paled in comparison to the madmen he played cards with and considered ‘friends’ – including a killer who blowtorched private parts.





And in many ways, the 56-year-old New Yorker is not like other gangsters.

This ‘wise guy’ was given an award in 10 Downing Street for his work with prisoners, has written several books and starred in a hit TV show.

But what really sets Big Lou apart from the other former mobsters that you see on true crime documentaries is that he never ‘snitched’ on his colleagues.

He maintained the omerta – the code of silence – rather than take a shorter prison sentence in return for providing information to the FBI back in 1996.

And while Ferrante is repentant for the torment he inflicted on his victims, he still holds ‘rats’ in contempt.

For him, it was the “treacherous” Salvatore ‘Sammy the Bull’ Gravano who almost brought down the Mafia.





Gravano, 81, only served five years in prison despite confessing to 19 murders, because he gave evidence in court against Gambino Godfather John Gotti in 1992.

It was to be the end of Gotti’s ‘Teflon Don’ reputation, with Sammy the Bull’s testimony helping send the gangster to the jail cell where he died in 2002.

Ferrante was at the home of John’s brother Pete Gotti shortly after he learned that Gravano had “gone sour” in 1991.

The gangster-turned-writer tells The Sun: “He knew that not only would it be the end of his brother but he also knew that’ll be the end of dozens of people who he had the potential to snitch on.

“It’s the moment the Mafia changed.

“That was a big turning point because all of the rats that came after always said time and again as soon as they made a deal with the government, I want a deal that’s as good as Sammy Gravano got.

“He set the precedent for a lot of the other rats to say, ‘Gee, I only killed 12 people. Why can’t I get the same five years he got? He killed 19.’

“That was a crucial moment and I was the absolute first one other than Pete to hear about it.”

Joyrider turned heist expert

Growing up in Queens in New York, Ferrante was more interested in joyriding than going to school.

It was a “fun” way of passing the time which led to far more serious crimes.



At first Ferrante sold parts from the stolen cars to backstreet repair garages, before progressing to thieving to order.

He recalls: “Instead of just stealing the cars for fun we could sell the parts. Then the body collision shops would give me an order, let’s say, ‘We need a 1989 Mercedes Benz in blue, we need parts for a 1987 Cadillac and a 1985 BMW.’ So I started to put together a crew of car thieves.”

When one of the mechanics told him how much their boxes full of tools were worth, Ferrante thought there would be more money in holding up the trucks that delivered these six-figure sum products.

Back then, he was a teenager who had no idea of the consequences of his actions, but instinctively tried to reassure the drivers whose goods he was about to unload.

Ferrante recalls: “I don’t want any of your readers to think I’m trying to say that I was nice to somebody as I was sticking a gun at their head, they’ll think I’m crazy.

“We did a bad thing but once we had him under control that’s when I said to him, ‘Look, I promise you we’ll drop you off, you’ll be fine. Is there anything in this truck you need that’s personal?’

“And he said to me, ‘There’s pictures of my family, my wife and kids, in there.’ He said, ‘Could you stick those in my pocket?’ We did.”

Serial killers

Naturally, these raids eventually caught up with Ferrante, but not before he became one of the Mafia’s go-to armed robbers.



He says: “Once you establish yourself as having a good crew that can pull off a heist and can pull off a hijack, rob a bank armoured car, once you establish yourself as a reliable crew you become extremely valuable to a Mafia family.”

Soon he found himself working for John Gotti, who took control of New York’s Gambino crime family in 1985, and other dangerous characters.

They included a hitman who took a blowtorch to the manhood of someone who had got on the wrong side of the mob.

Ferrante says: “There were a number of Mafia killers who exhibit the traits of serial killers, traits of the most perverse killers where they do things that do not need to be done.

I had friends who cut peoples’ heads off Louis Ferrante

“There are some Mafa killers who cut off penises. This particular guy, in this incident, he blowtorched someone’s penis off.

“If I was in a room with them, I got along with them. I might have played cards with them. I may have talked to them, but I wasn’t there when they did those things.

“I had friends who cut people’s heads off. Would I have a friend like that today? Absolutely not, I wouldn’t want to be anywhere near anyone who cuts people’s heads off.”

These killers let everyone know they were not to be crossed, and Ferrante will never forget one particular monster who even presented a decapitated head as a warning shot.

He continues: “Apparently he brought it to a bar and placed the head on a bar.

“I guess he wanted to show everybody whoever he had a problem with that this is what happened to my last enemy, you know, be careful what you do.”



Did the crime, did the time

Ferrante was accused of shooting another man in the leg, but his eventual convictions were for fraud and robbery.

He insists: “There’s no way I can kill somebody, especially one of my friends, somebody I know, for all the money in the world.

“That’s not to say I wasn’t capable of violence, I was. I wasn’t afraid to defend myself and my friends.”

He also would never “betray” one of his friends.

Rather than cooperate with the authorities, Ferrante pleaded guilty in 1997 to a series of robberies and was handed a 13-year prison sentence.

There’s no way I can kill somebody… That’s not to say I wasn’t capable of violence, I was Louis Ferrante

Explaining why he never informed on his fellow criminals, he says: “These are my friends. I knew their families. How do you just throw them under the bus to save yourself?”

Ferrante, who gained notoriety for rapping on a song called Justice Not Found: The John Gotti Story, is particularly aggrieved by Gravano’s duplicity.

Sammy the Bull worked his way up to become Gotti’s underboss by bumping off other gangsters.



He claims: “Sammy the Bull Gravano killed most of his victims because he wanted something from them. I didn’t like that.”

Machete murders in prison

It was going to prison that helped turn Ferrante’s life around.

When he entered the correctional facility he was “obviously illiterate” and “hadn’t picked up a book to read in my life”.

Spending days on end in his cell led him to devour books and to learn the meaning of words along the way.

Ferrante continues: “When I read those books, I understood nothing of what I read. My vocabulary wasn’t good enough to even get through a paragraph so it was confusing to me.

“Eventually I bought a dictionary in jail with stamps. I was determined to look up the definition of every single word that I did not know.”

People were killing each other with machetes Louis Ferrante

The inmate also came to feel remorse for the fear he’d brought to the world.

Ferrante says: “When I contemplated in prison I understood that there is such a thing as natural justice and karma and I was suffering from it when I was in prison.”

The maximum security prison in Lewisburg in Pennsylvania was not the place anyone would want to be.

He recalls: “People were killing each other with machetes. The Aryan Brotherhood were at war with the black Muslims and the Aryan brotherhood had hacked to death two black Muslims on the very first day I had arrived on the compound.



“People were telling me you could be targeted. I said, ‘Why? I’m Italian American.’

“They said, well, the problem is the Aryans hate you too because they hate everybody.”

Fresh start

Ferrante studied law and got his sentence reduced to eight years.

When he was released in 2003 he became an author, writing books including Mob Rules, Unlocked: The Life and Crimes of a Mafia Insider and his latest, the Borgata Trilogy.

Ferrante visited prisons, including British ones, to encourage inmates to improve their literacy.

As a result he was given a Celebrity Reading Hero Award by Sarah Brown at Downing Street.

He says: “The Brits were really good to me.”

He also promoted more cordial relations, telling prisoners that guards “want nothing more than for you to get out of here and start a better life for yourself”.

In 2013 he hosted the Discovery Channel show Inside The Gangster’s Code and has now written a history of the American Mafia.

Ferrante believes part of the reason Italians formed such tight and often violent bonds when they arrived in the United States was because they were persecuted.



He says: “I did not know until I researched for my trilogy that the Italians were the second largest ethnic group to be lynched in the United States.”

Nevertheless, prejudice does not excuse their actions, in his opinion.

Ferrante concludes: “There are plenty of Italian Americans who were discriminated against, but still chose to work hard and prospered in America.”

Lou Ferrante’s new book Borgata is released on April 7 from bookshops and Amazon.

News.title: Man jailed for life after murdering 'kind' girlfriend who 'fought to stay alive'
News.content:
Man jailed for life after murdering 'kind' girlfriend who 'fought to stay alive'

Norbert Maiksner told a police officer about the murder after he was found wandering the M40 motorway

View 2 Images Norbert Maiksner told a police officer about the murder after he was found wandering the M40 motorway (Image: PA)

An 'evil' man murdered his girlfriend who 'struggled to stay alive' in her last moments.

‌



Norbert Maiksner, 49, of Polish descent, was convicted following a trial at Portsmouth Crown Court of the murder of 45-year-old Frances Obiefuleh at their home in Havant, Hampshire.

‌



The killer was also charged with child neglect. According to reports Maiksner has been jailed for life to serve a minimum of 24 years, after he suffocated his girlfriend by wrapping tape around her face.

‌



Paul Cavin KC, prosecuting, told the trial that the defendant was found by a Highways Officer walking along the hard shoulder of the M40 motorway near High Wycombe, Buckinghamshire, on the morning of April 17 2025.

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

Maiksner told the officer that they should call the police because he had killed his girlfriend. Mr Cavin said that a post-mortem examination revealed that Ms Obiefuleh died of smothering with injuries caused by compression of the neck and chest.

‌



Mr Cavin said that the defendant also had scratches to his chest and back, and added: "The likely and frankly terrible conclusion is that they were inflicted by Frances with her fingers and fingernails during the attack by the defendant in her last moments as she struggled to stay alive."

View 2 Images Family said: "Frances was kind, intelligent, and resourceful" (Image: Family Handout/PA)

A Hampshire Constabulary spokesman said that Maiksner had not attended the trial and it had gone ahead in his absence.

‌



The force spokesman said: "During his trial the court heard that Maiksner had told officers that he had killed Frances and stated that it was all a dream and that he wanted to wake up."

Detective Sergeant Heather Kenwright said: "I am glad to see Maiksner face a life behind bars for committing the most heinous and evil of acts, it is what he deserves for taking the life of an innocent woman. He has caused such unthinkable suffering to both Frances in the last moments of her life, and to her family, who have had their loved one taken from them so brutally and must now try to rebuild their lives without her.

"My thoughts remain with Frances's family, and whilst no sentence can ever truly bring them justice for the tragic loss of Frances's life, I hope it brings them some semblance of closure to know that Maiksner is now facing the consequences of his abhorrent actions."

Article continues below

Paying tribute to Ms Obiefuleh, her family said in a statement released through police: "Frances was kind, intelligent, and resourceful - a caring and deeply loving mother, sister, aunt, and friend to many. She was a devoted mother and beautiful in every sense of the word.

"Someone we love has been cruelly taken from us, and it has changed our lives forever. We have lost a truly beautiful soul.

"Her bright light has been cruelly dimmed, and we are left shaken, heartbroken, and still trying to process the grief and shock of losing Frances."

News.title: Iran war LIVE: Tolls approved for Strait of Hormuz as 'Americans prohibited'
News.content:
Iran has confirmed an approval for tolls in the Strait of Hormuz, warning they plan to prohibit 'Americans and the Zionist regime from passage'.

Writing on Telegram, they said the plans will also allow for safety of naval vessels, as well as the prohibition of countries participating in unilateral sanctions against Iran.

This came as Donald Trump threatened to "completely obliterate" Iran's Kharg Island and the country's power plants if the Strait of Hormuz is not "immediately open for business". It comes as two major international airports have been impacted following further Iranian drone attacks overnight.

"If the Hormuz Strait is not immediately 'Open for Business,' we will conclude our lovely 'stay' in Iran by blowing up and completely obliterating all of their Electric Generating Plants, Oil Wells and Kharg Island (and possibly all desalinization plants!), which we have purposefully not yet 'touched,'" Trump said in a post on Truth Social today.

News.title: Water companies breached eco rules an incredible 3,000 times, watchdogs say
News.content:
Water companies breached eco rules an incredible 3,000 times, watchdogs say

The Environment Agency says they have bolstered their inspection team in a bid to assess treatment works, sewage pumping stations and storm overflows after completing 10,000 checks in the past year

View 3 Images Inspections sparked more than 3,000 demands for improvements issued to water companies, including repairing sewage works (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Watchdogs exposed more than 3,000 breaches of environmental rules by water companies as they staged a crackdown.

‌



The Environment Agency said it had expanded its inspections of treatment works, sewage pumping stations and storm overflows, completing more than 10,000 checks of water company assets in the past year.

‌



Inspection teams uncovered more than 3,000 permit condition breaches, where companies are failing to comply with environmental legislation.

‌



It sparked more than 3,000 demands for improvements issued to water companies, including repairing sewage works and upgrading infrastructure, the EA said.

The agency said permit conditions could be breached for a number of reasons, such as equipment failure, effluent not meeting water quality standards, not treating the required amount of wastewater or failing to manage the water and sewage network in line with permit requirements.

View 3 Images Sewage leaks have a devastating effect on wildlife and water companies are coming under intense pressure to invest in their systems (Image: PA)

‌



It comes as more funding and 500 additional staff have allowed the Environment Agency to undertake far more inspections, up from 4,600 in 2024/2025 to more than 10,000 this financial year.

And the EA suggests its greater scrutiny of water companies is having an effect on making them manage their assets more responsibly, with 22% of site visits uncovering at least one issue this year — down from 25% the previous year.

Helen Wakeham, director for water at the Environment Agency, said: "In our role as regulators of the water industry, we are changing how we operate — with better data, record levels of new staff and greater powers to do our job effectively. Inspections are a vital preventative measure, with our teams issuing over 3,000 individual actions to water companies, including repairing sewage works and upgrading infrastructure.

‌



"Together, this will drive meaningful improvements in performance, hold persistent offenders to account and ultimately create a cleaner water environment." Water minister Emma Hardy added: "Thanks to our investment in the Environment Agency, inspectors are out in force, checking water company assets at unprecedented levels and taking action where standards aren't met.

"This greater oversight of water companies coupled with our long-term reforms will prevent problems before they occur and ensure serial offenders are punished, ensuring a healthy, sustainable water system for the future."

View 3 Images James Wallace, chief executive of campaign group River Action said 'inspections alone will not solve the problem'

‌



James Wallace, chief executive of campaign group River Action, said water companies had discharged more than 1.8 million hours of sewage into rivers, lakes and seas in 2025, while most of England's 35 inland bathing sites were unsafe for swimming.

"It is good to see the Government getting serious about water quality, but inspections alone will not fix the problem. With prosecutions taking years to reach court and fines far too low, water polluters are not being properly held to account.

"The upcoming Water Reform Bill is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reset the system. The Government must take back control of water company ownership and ensure bill payers' money cleans up rivers, not investor pockets," he urged.

Article continues below

Richard Benwell, chief executive of environmental coalition Wildlife and Countryside Link, said: "It's good that inspection numbers have doubled, but the scale of lawbreaking is alarming. Thousands of breaches in a single year show that pollution is business as usual for water companies."

He warned that enforcement remained too slow and weak and said: "When the new water regulator is set up, it must be empowered to act decisively — inspecting more assets, including the condition of nature on company land, and handing down rapid, significant penalties, including criminal sanctions where needed."

News.title: Iran approves toll plans for Strait of Hormuz as 'Americans prohibited from passage'
News.content:
Iran is set to impose tolls on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

The announcement also said that 'Americans and the Zionist regime' would be barred from the crucial waterway.

The news came less than two hours after the White House once again insisted it was in talks with Tehran, with Iranian officials breaking the news in a post on Telegram this evening.

The post, titled "Approval of the plan to impose tolls on the Strait of Hormuz in the Parliament's Security Commission" was shared by the official Fars news agency and said the "the Strait of Hormuz management plan" had been announced by a member of the National Security Commission.

This plan would mean that ships passing through the Iranian-controlled strait would be forced to pay a toll. The news comes after multiple ship have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz since the start of US-Israeli strikes on Iran a month ago.

"The key points of this plan are as follows," the post read, before listing:

"Security arrangements for the strait.

"Safety of naval vessels.

"Environmental issues.

"Financial arrangements and toll systems in rials.

"Prohibition of Americans and the Zionist regime from passage.

"Enforcement of Iran's sovereign role and the armed forces.

"Cooperation of the esteemed country of Oman in the legal regime structure.

"Prohibition of countries participating in unilateral sanctions against Iran."

The news comes hours after a White House press briefing saw Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt insist that talks between the US and Iran are going well and remain under way.

This is despite multiple statements from Iranian officials that talks with the US were not ongoing. Leavitt explained this as Iranian officials "public posturing" adding that private discussions with the Iranians are "much different".

The press secretary was asked a question by the Wall Street Journal about how the objectives laid out by the administration will lead to re-opening the Strait of Hormuz.

In response Leavitt laid out the four “core objectives” of the war as: destroying the Iranian Navy, destroying their ballistic missiles, dismantling their defence industrial infrastructure that produces those weapons and preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

“The full-reopening of the strait is something the administration is working towards but the core objectives of the operation have been clearly defined for the American people by the commander in chief,” Leavitt added.

Image: Getty Images) Getty Images)

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei acknowledged that Tehran had been given a 15-point proposal from the Trump administration, but said there had been no direct negotiations with Washington so far.

Earlier, Iran’s parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, dismissed the talks in Pakistan as a cover to get more US troops into the area.

Twice during Mr Trump’s second term, the US has attacked Iran while in the middle of negotiations, once with the strikes on February 28 that started the current war and also in June 2025.

Mr Qalibaf said Iranian forces were “waiting for the arrival of American troops on the ground to set them on fire and punish their regional partners forever”, according to state media.

The US has already launched airstrikes once that targeted military positions on Kharg.

Iran has threatened to launch its own ground invasion of Gulf Arab countries and mine the Persian Gulf if US troops land on its territory.

To get an amphibious invasion force to Kharg would mean transiting the Strait of Hormuz and most of the Persian Gulf.

Experts say that holding the island would also be a challenge, because in addition to its missiles and drones, it would be well within artillery range from the Iranian mainland.

News.title: Thousands of pounds raised for 16-year-old girl 'taken too soon'
News.content:
Thousands of pounds raised for 16-year-old girl 'taken too soon'

Chloe Watson died in the street despite the valiant efforts of locals - now floral tributes have been left at the spot where she died and a fundraiser has been launched to give her the 'best send off possible'

View 4 Images Tributes have been paid to Chloe Watson, including flowers with the message 'my beautiful girl' (Image: gofundme.com)

Wellwishers have donated £12,000 to the family of a 16-year-old girl described as a 'beautiful soul taken too soon’.

‌



Chloe Watson was killed by a wound to the back over the weekend and died in the street despite the valiant efforts of locals. Floral tributes have been left at the spot in Kennerleigh Avenue, Crossgates, in Leeds, West Yorkshire, where Chloe died.

‌



And her cousin launched a Gofundme page which stands at £11,943. Grief-stricken Shantelle, 22, wrote:” I’m setting up a go fund me for my 16 year old cousin who’s life was sadly taken in tragedy, 16 years young didn’t even make it to her 18th.

‌



View 4 Images Chloe Watson, who died at the weekend aged just 16 (Image: Leeds Live/MEN MEDIA)

“Her whole life was taken in a flash over a boy, her mum is distraught she has left two younger siblings behind. I wanted to create a go fund me to help give her the best send off possible she didn’t deserve this she was so full of life such an innocent beautiful soul taken too soon.”

Amongst the floral tributes in the street was a heartfelt message to "my beautiful girl" saying: "Rest easy my Chloe. Love you forever my crazy girl."

‌



A photo of the teenager has also been taped to a box on the roadside alongside the growing collection of flowers and messages. Forensic investigators continue to work at the scene in Kennerleigh Avenue.

View 4 Images Chloe Watson, who died in a street attack (Image: UKNIP)

Another person left a toy at the scene and told the BBC Chloe used to play with his dog when they were younger. Looking at the floral tributes, local resident Gillian Brook said: "This area's really quiet. This young girl's lost her life. She'd got all her life ahead of her.

Article continues below

"My granddaughter's the same age. My heart goes out to her family and everybody who knew her. It's devastating. It's just a really quiet area and you don't expect it. It's so, so sad."

View 4 Images Floral tributes at the spot where Chloe died (Image: PA)

Det Ch Supt Marc Bowes, senior investigating officer, said on Sunday that inquiries into the teenager's death were continuing. He appealed for anyone who was in the Kennerleigh Avenue area in the early hours of Saturday morning to "come forward if they have any information which could assist our investigation"

News.title: Body of newborn found in portable toilet near Waffle House
News.content:
Body of newborn found in portable toilet near Waffle House

The woman allegedly walked into the restaurant and told staff she had given birth in a nearby portable toilet

View Image (Image: Google)

The body of a new-born baby boy was found inside a portable toilet near a popular restaurant chain, authorities revealed the baby was "alive at birth".

The grim discovery was made in Louisiana, United States near Waffle House in Gretna, a suburb of New Orleans.

Emergency services were called to the area in the early hours of last Thursday morning (March 26). According to Express, a woman allegedly walked into the restaurant and told staff she had given birth in a nearby portable toilet.

Police and paramedics were dispatched to the Waffle House at 52 West Bank Expressway at around 3.17am local time. Officers later found the baby boy’s body in the tank of a porta-potty at a construction site near the Mississippi river at 62 West Bank Expressway, around a block away.

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as your Preferred Source in your Google search settings.

Gretna Police Deputy Chief Jason DiMarco said: "The autopsy showed the baby was alive at birth."

According to the Jefferson Parish Coroner’s Office, the infant’s body was discovered in liquid cleaning chemicals inside the portable toilet tank. An autopsy found the baby died from asphyxia by drowning.

The coroner’s office said the new-born weighed 7.2lbs and had been born during the third trimester of his mother’s pregnancy. Tim Genevay, director of forensic operations for the coroner’s office, said the baby had not been given a name.

Officials said the infant is likely to receive a 'pauper's burial' unless relatives come forward before the end of April. This refers to a basic funeral paid for by the state or local authority when a person dies and there are no relatives able or willing to arrange or pay for it.

Article continues below

Police believe the child’s mother was homeless at the time she gave birth. Louisiana’s Safe Haven Law allows parents to hand over custody of a new-born up to 60 days old without facing prosecution.

Under the law, babies can be left at hospitals, fire stations, police stations or public health units without the risk of being prosecuted for abandonment. The babies can then be treated at hospital.

Lise Naccari, founder of Compassionate Burials for Indigent Babies, said: "It’s very important that mothers know they can use the Safe Haven Law."

News.title: Andrew's 'shameful' Royal Lodge exit truth revealed as King orders home clear out
News.content:
Andrew's 'shameful' Royal Lodge exit truth revealed as King orders home clear out

Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has reportedly been given a stern ultimatum by his elder brother King Charles as he adjusts to his reduced life at Sandringham, with his former staff at Royal Lodge working around the clock to clear away any trace of him

View 3 Images Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor faces yet another blow as he adjusts to life away from Royal Lodge (Image: Tom Maddick SWNS)

For years, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor lived in the lap of luxury at the 30-bedroom Royal Lodge, with servants attending to his every eccentric whim.

‌



Now these same servants have been tasked with scouring the Windsor mansion of every trace of the disgraced former prince, clearing out any lingering possessions, and even burning their own belongings. This fervent spring clean was reportedly demanded by Andrew's elder brother, King Charles III, who has made his position on his troublesome middle sibling's living arrangements crystal clear.

‌



Last month, Charles, 77, brought forward a deadline for Andrew, 66, to leave the Windsor estate behind after he was repeatedly named in the latest tranche of files relating to convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein, who died behind bars in 2019. Andrew has vehemently and consistently denied any wrongdoing in connection with sex offender Epstein, with whom he was friends for a number of years.

‌



Swept away from the grandeur of Royal Lodge in the middle of the night, Andrew now temporarily resides at Wood Farm on the Sandringham Estate, where he awaits the completion of renovations at the boggy and secluded Marsh Farm, which will serve as his more permanent residence.

While a charming home in the eyes of most, there's no doubt that this is a significant downgrade for the favourite son of a monarch, born to expect rather than sinply strive to a life of opulence. And to add insult to injury, Andrew has reportedly been ordered to ensure Royal Lodge is completely cleared out by the weekend, in yet another ultimatum by Charles.

Prince Harry issued stark warning after claims he wants to bring kids to see King in UK READ MORE :

View 3 Images The once bustling Royal Lodge now has a desolate appearance (Image: NO CREDIT)

‌



In the past few days, it's understood that Royal aides have been working against the clock to strip the sprawling grace-and-favour home of its remaining possessions, from the grand reception rooms to the staff quarters. Various skips have been loaded and removed from the historic estate, with removal vans spotted coming and going.

One source previously told the Mirror:“Andrew was told everything had to be out and absolutely nothing was to be left behind. He hasn’t been back to collect anything, leaving staff to Everything has to be out by the weekend, and we’ve been told no trace of the former occupants or staff should remain.”

Staff have even been setting fire to their own unwanted belongings, as the memories of the York family's time at Royal Lodge quite literally go up in smoke. On Tuesday, March 24, a man, understood to have once served as Andrew's valet, was seen burning household items, including furniture, on the sweeping grounds.

‌



View 3 Images Skips and removal vans were spotted in Windsor, and the pressure is said to be on (Image: NO CREDIT)

Once a bustling royal household, the Royal Lodge estate is now a desolate place, with guards notably absent from the usually staffed gatehouse. Aerial photos show a filled skip, close to the rear of the residence, with another yellow-coloured skip visible at the front of the estate, just behind the front gates.

Back in December, it emerged that Andrew would likely not be getting any compensation after vacating Royal Lodge under a cloud of shame. BBC News reported at the time that, under his leasing arrangement, Andrew could have been entitled to £488,000 if he chose to surrender his 75-year lease within 25 years, but this clause all depended on the property being well-maintained. However, a report from the Crown Estate for MPs determined that the condition of Royal Lodge is "not out of keeping with a tenancy of this duration", with the cost of repairing "dilapidations" meaning any return of advance payments would be unlikely.

Article continues below

Andrew took on the lengthy lease of Royal Lodge in 2003, paying more than £8.5 million up-front to cover the costs of renovation, as well as to avoid any rent requirements, based on a notional annual rent of £260,000. As part of this arrangement, Andrew had to pay a token "peppercorn" payment, standard practice for long leases as per the Crown Estate, on occasions when an advance payment is given.

News.title: Siblings face £250k bill after neighbours' 'systematic destruction' tree claim
News.content:
Siblings face £250k bill after neighbours' 'systematic destruction' tree claim

Robert and Amanda McCarthy are seeking £250,000 in court over what they have claimed was the 'systematic destruction' of Leylandii trees at their home in Nazeing, Essex

View 4 Images Robert McCarthy and his wife claimed their neighbours destroyed their property by tearing down the leylandii trees (Image: Champion News)

Siblings could could be left with a "ruinous" quarter-of-a-million-pound court bill after invading their neighbours' "immaculate" garden and hacking down their 33-foot Leylandii trees.

Robert McCarthy and his wife Amanda lived for years in "relative harmony" alongside their neighbour, Foulla Bowler, and the two siblings she owns her house with. But a row over the boundary between their gardens broke out in 2018, and the couple sued over a row of 33-foot-tall Leylandii trees which were removed over "overshadowing" complaints.

Mrs Bowler, her brother John Barberis and sister Mary Englishby pulled out their back fence and had tree surgeons remove the trees, which the suing couple claimed in court amounted to "systematic destruction".

Lawyer explains what to do if neighbours break new March 31 bin rules READ MORE :

View 4 Images A court found the neighbours had trespassed on the couple's property to cut the trees down (Image: Getty Images)

The couple told Central London County Court the "systematic destruction" of their garden in the village of Nazeing, Essex, had completely ruined the privacy of their home, demanding almost £250,000 in costs and damages. Following a trial, Judge Alan Saggerson has now ruled in favour of the couple on the location of the boundary, finding that the siblings had "trespassed" into their neighbours' garden to hack down the trees.

The trio had taken "unilateral action to re-order the disputed boundary" between the properties amid what he called "fence wars" between the neighbours.

The full cost of the case to the siblings will be decided later, but the decision means they are likely to be liable for the McCarthys' lawyers' bills, which are estimated at £130,000, on top of their own significant court costs - plus potentially as much as £115,000 in compensation.

"This is a protracted and potentially ruinous boundary dispute between neighbours," said the judge in his judgment, which was only made public last week.

During the trial last October, the judge was told that civil construction manager Mr McCarthy, 59, and his carer wife, Amanda, 61, bought their home in Common View, Bumbles Green, Nazeing, in 2001. The house, which Mrs McCarthy said had an "immaculate, very pleasant garden" when they moved in, is bordered to the rear by the home of Mrs Bowler, 61, known as Kormakitis.

It had been Mrs Bowler's family home as a teenager, but she now lives there with her own family and it is owned by her, along with her two siblings, John Barberis, 63, and Mary Englishby, 59.

Barrister Christopher Coyle, for the McCarthys, told the judge that the two gardens were divided by a fence, with a row of Leylandii trees on the McCarthys' side. However, a bitter boundary dispute erupted around 2018, with Mrs Bowler and her siblings claiming the dividing line was actually beyond the fence, putting the Leylandii on their land.

View 4 Images The decision means the siblings are likely to be liable for the McCarthys' lawyers' bills (Image: Champion News)

And, despite knowing that there was a dispute, Mrs Bowler had in 2018 applied for permission to fell 29 trees, before the family went ahead with the plan, cutting down most of them in January 2022.

Mr Coyle said the felling work had continued into a second day even though the McCarthys wrote to the siblings via lawyers to request them to stop cutting. Giving evidence, Mr McCarthy described it as an "invasion" and complained of a "relentless destruction of my garden," telling the judge: "This is how we feel as a family."

"I can stand upstairs in my house and they can see me walking around," he said from the witness box. "I want my privacy back like I had."

He said that, when the couple bought the house, they were led to believe that the fence beyond the trees was the boundary, making the trees part of their property. The trees were well-established when we moved in," he told the judge. "We thought the chain link fence was the boundary as it ran along. I had no reason not to believe that to be the boundary."

The McCarthys sued for about £115,000 in compensation, including £73,500 to plant new trees and restore their privacy, as well as a declaration that the true boundary is the line of the old fence.

But Mrs Bowler and her siblings insisted that they had every right to remove the fence and trees as they were in fact on their land, and that they removed them due to "overshadowing" and potential damage to their land. Her brother, Mr Barberis, said he was there in 1981 when their father, Elias Barberis, discussed buying Kormakitis and remembers hearing that the boundary was several feet beyond the fence. It was his father who had planted the trees.

"Some of the trees are missing, not all of them," he added, when pressed on their felling. "These are trees that we planted and a fence that we put up."

"I clearly remember our parents giving [the previous owner] permission to trim our trees from his side to stop them overshadowing his garden." Giving judgment, Judge Saggerson said the siblings' evidence was "less reliable and less accurate" than the McCarthys', but did not find they were lying, but instead had "persuaded themselves of the righteousness of their own case."

He said the chain link fence had been there in 1981 and was probably there at the latest in 1975, with wooden panels later put in place along it.

‌



However, he said he did not accept that the siblings' father had been told when buying Kormakitis in 1981 that his land extended 6ft beyond the line of the fence. "I do not accept that he had any reasonable grounds for believing this, although over the passage of many years he may have persuaded himself that this was the position," he said.

View 4 Images Mrs Bowler and the siblings claimed the Leylandii were on their land (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

"Unfortunately, as I find, the defendants took unilateral action to re-order the disputed boundary." Their father, with his son John present, had begun by starting to take the fence down in May 2018, with plants then being pulled up in the face of objections from Mr McCarthy.

‌



Despite a replacement fence being put up by Mr McCarthy, the siblings again removed it in May the following year, before removing another in February 2020.

"On 3 March 2020, a tree surgeon instructed by the defendants attended and started removing trees from their garden and also started taking out other planting along the disputed boundary," said the judge. "In early January 2022, the tree surgeons returned. They cut down the remaining trees along the disputed boundary, completely removing the privacy screen that had existed for so many years.

"Due to the defendants' unilateral action, the landscape along the disputed boundary has completely changed from that which existed before May 2018."

Article continues below

Having heard expert evidence, he said the original fence line was the "true boundary," placing the Leylandii trees in the McCarthys' garden. That tallied with the historic attitude and behaviour of the two sets of neighbours in respect of the boundary, he said, finding that all of them, plus Elias Barberis, from 2001 to 2018 had "conducted themselves on the clear basis that the fence represented their mutual north-south boundary."

"It was the defendants' unilateral action from May 2018 that disrupted what had been settled for decades," he said. "It follows that Mr and Mrs McCarthy's claims for trespass...are established on the balance of probabilities."

The case is set to return to court in the summer for a hearing to decide the consequences of the ruling against the siblings, including any compensation due and the costs of the case.
